## Artifacts in this pack (16 of 26 in unit `governance`)

### `CNF-001` — Committed projected artifacts differ from what project.js generates
- **conflict** · status **open** · severity high
- **statement:** Running `node _registry/project.js` rewrites all 93 committed artifacts (374 insertions, 95 deletions on 2026-10-22): a changed constitutional notice in every file, and `Owns: Digital Twins`→`Digital Twin`, `Owns: Agents`→`Agent` in two. Neither audit.js nor CI regenerates and compares, so the drift is invisible.
- **evidence:** reproduce: node _registry/project.js && git diff --stat (then git checkout -- . to restore)
- **evidence:** measured continuously: `node _registry/context.js hygiene` → derived-drift (metric derivedDrift)
- **between:** _registry/project.js
- **decision needed:** Either re-project and commit the 93 artifacts (the generator is the authority under Law 003), or revert the generator text. Kept separate from this change: regenerating 93 documents is out of scope for an unrelated fix.
- **proposed resolution:** Re-project in its own reviewed commit, then add the DERIVED_DRIFT hygiene check to the ratchet so it can never recur.

### `CNF-002` — The registry seal hashes a file that does not exist
- **conflict** · status **open** · severity high
- **statement:** lib/canonical.js INPUT_FILES names `UCOS-Zero-Hardcoding-Constitution.md`; the parser (lib/ucos.js) reads `UCRS-Zero-Hardcoding-Constitution.md`. The seal manifest records the named file as missing on both sides, so edits to the real corpus never drift the seal. This may be the previously identified G1 seal fix; it is kept separate from this change.
- **evidence:** lib/canonical.js INPUT_FILES vs lib/ucos.js DOCS entry `ucrs`
- **evidence:** `npm run registry` reports `drift: none` while the real file is outside the manifest
- **between:** lib/canonical.js; UCRS-Zero-Hardcoding-Constitution.md
- **decision needed:** Approve the one-line input-name fix (the G1 seal fix) as its own change.
- **proposed resolution:** Correct the INPUT_FILES entry; once it lands this acknowledgement must be removed and the dangling edge disappears.
- **acknowledges finding:** DANGLING_EDGE on `UCOS-Zero-Hardcoding-Constitution.md`

### `CNF-003` — Documents marked SUPERSEDED are live compile inputs
- **conflict** · status **open** · severity medium
- **statement:** Three root documents declare `do not derive implementations from this file`, yet lib/canonical.js compiles them into the runtime registry. Their authority is ambiguous: provenance (per their banner) or declaration source (per the compiler).
- **evidence:** banner at the top of each file
- **evidence:** lib/canonical.js INPUT_FILES
- **between:** class=constitutional-corpus, pathGlob=UCOS-Constitutional-*.md|UCRS-*.md; lib/canonical.js
- **decision needed:** Declare whether superseded documents may remain declaration sources; if yes, re-word the banner; if no, remove them from INPUT_FILES after migrating what the runtime still reads from them.
- **proposed resolution:** Owner decision.

- **conflict** · status **open** · severity medium
- **statement:** The README and audit.js treat Laws 001–005 as binding, but their text exists only in a document marked SUPERSEDED. The registry (the declared single source of truth) carries no machine-readable law entries.

- **evidence:** UCOS-Constitutional-Master-Architecture.md § FUNDAMENTAL LAWS
- **between:** UCOS-Constitutional-Master-Architecture.md; _registry/primitives.json
- **decision needed:** Whether to add the laws to the registry (registry schema change, governed) so constraints can quote an active-canonical source.
- **proposed resolution:** Add a `laws` array to an existing registry file through the governance process; then re-point LAW-00x constraints.

### `CNF-005` — Two pipelines, one declared source of truth
- **conflict** · status **open** · severity medium
- **statement:** README/UCOS-REPOSITORY-INDEX say `_registry/*.json` is the single source of truth and documents are projections (project.js). lib/canonical.js says the sealed canonical.lxr is `THE runtime source of truth`, compiled from the same registry JSON plus corpora and console code. Precedence between the two outputs is not declared anywhere.
- **evidence:** README.md § The one idea
- **evidence:** lib/canonical.js header
- **evidence:** _registry/compile.js header
- **between:** _registry/project.js; _registry/compile.js
- **decision needed:** Record that both are projections of the same inputs (registry JSON + corpora) and that neither output is an input to the other.
- **proposed resolution:** Adopt the statement above as a decision; the context graph already models both outputs as derived-from the same sources.
